source.title: Maximum Points in an Archery Competition

teaching.hint: How many arrows are useful in a section once you have decided whether to win it?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A won section needs only Alice count plus one, while any additional arrows give no extra score; the decision is a small subset of wins.
solution_outline.approach: Enumerate section subsets, sum their minimum winning costs and point values, and retain a highest-value subset whose cost fits. Assign its minimum arrows and place all leftover arrows in section zero.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Each inspected subset has its exact minimal resource cost and attainable points; the current best has maximum value among feasible subsets inspected so far.
solution_outline.correctness: Every allocation has a set of won positive sections and spends at least their minimum costs. Exhaustive subsets therefore bound its score. Conversely a feasible subset can be realized by minimum winning allocations and leftover arrows in section zero, which cannot change point value. The best feasible subset attains the upper bound.
solution_outline.complexity: O(12 * 2^12) time and O(12) space, independent of arrow magnitude.
solution_outline.pitfall: Using only the minimum winning allocation without placing leftover arrows violates the exact output budget.

common_wrong_turns: Using only the minimum winning allocation without placing leftover arrows violates the exact output budget.
source_fidelity_notes: Removed scoring diagrams and Alice reward details irrelevant to Bob objective; retained strict win threshold, exact budget, and any optimal allocation.
